construction-readiness.note: OSHA's Focus Four training covers falls, struck-by, caught-in/between, and electrocution hazards. Use it to recognize hazards and ask for the site's required controls.

For construction unprotected sides and edges within 29 CFR 1926.501(b)(1), the rule generally requires specified fall protection at 6 feet or more above a lower level. Other tasks have separate provisions; do not apply one threshold to every situation.

carpentry-fundamentals.note: Use supervised training and the task-specific site controls. This reference is hazard-awareness guidance, not a structural design or operating procedure.

electrical-foundations.note: In covered general-industry work, 29 CFR 1910.333 addresses deenergizing and work practices; only qualified persons may work on energized parts under its provisions. Construction work also has its own standards. Introductory study does not qualify a learner for live work.

plumbing-foundations.note: This reference supports jobsite hazard awareness. Actual plumbing design, permits, backflow protection, and licensing must be verified with the local authority and qualified supervisor; OSHA training is not a plumbing license.

hvac-foundations.note: EPA Section 608 requires the appropriate certification for covered stationary-equipment work that could release refrigerants. Verify the activity and certification type; this course is not Section 608 certification.

General-industry servicing covered by 29 CFR 1910.147 requires a hazardous-energy control program, procedures, and training. The standard has exclusions; electrical hazards and construction may fall under other provisions. Follow the employer's applicable procedure.

painting-drywall.note: Paid work disturbing paint in covered pre-1978 housing or child-occupied facilities can trigger lead-safe certification, training, and work-practice requirements. Exceptions and authorized state programs matter; Georgia operates an authorized program. Verify before disturbing paint.

Construction hazard communication incorporates the requirements of 29 CFR 1910.1200. Use the actual chemical label, safety data sheet, and employer training; do not improvise mixtures or exposure controls.

masonry-fundamentals.note: Covered construction tasks involving respirable crystalline silica require appropriate exposure controls under 29 CFR 1926.1153. Table 1 addresses specified tasks and conditions; otherwise the exposure-assessment route may apply. A generic dust mask or visible-dust check does not establish compliance.

welding-foundations.note: 29 CFR 1926.353 sets ventilation and protection requirements for covered construction welding, cutting, and heating, including material- and location-specific provisions. The employer must determine the controls; this lesson does not authorize hot work.

cdl-preparation.note: ELDT applies to specified first-time Class A or B licenses, upgrades, and certain endorsements. Verify applicability, registered provider requirements, and state prerequisites. TCF preparation is not registered ELDT or a license.

Applicable Class A/B and passenger/school-bus training includes theory and behind-the-wheel requirements through registered providers before the relevant state skills tests; state rules may add requirements.

For covered property-carrying operations, the basic limits include 11 driving hours after 10 consecutive hours off duty and a 14-hour driving window. A 30-minute interruption is generally required after 8 cumulative driving hours without such an interruption. Exceptions, weekly limits, and other provisions apply; passenger rules differ.

facilities-maintenance.note: Covered general-industry servicing may require the employer's hazardous-energy control procedures under 29 CFR 1910.147. Determine the actual task, scope, and applicable standard; a maintenance title does not establish authorization.

For covered workplaces, hazard communication addresses labels, safety data sheets, written programs, and employee information and training. Use the exact product information and the employer's applicable controls.

digital-literacy.note: NIST's small-business guidance supports securing accounts, devices, and data. Use approved tools and policies; guidance is not a guarantee that a device or transaction is safe.
CISA recommends MFA and moving toward phishing-resistant methods. Availability and recovery options differ by service; never approve an unexpected authentication request.

email-communication.note: Use approved channels, minimum necessary information, and verified recipients. NIST security guidance supports these habits; specific privacy and retention duties depend on the organization and data.

office-documents.note: Excel formulas use operators, references, and functions; an equals sign begins a formula. Check the exact ranges, reference behavior, and application version. Sample calculations here use invented values.

it-support.note: NIST guidance supports controlled access, secure configuration, and careful data handling. Follow the employer's authorization and incident procedures; a support request does not grant unlimited access.

networking-fundamentals.note: Use the client-server model to distinguish devices, requests, responses, and network services. This is a technical learning reference, not permission to scan or alter a live network.
Use approved network controls and access boundaries; do not disable protection or expand access as an undocumented troubleshooting shortcut.

cybersecurity-basics.note: Use NIST security guidance to build repeatable prevention and reporting habits. Security depends on implementation and context; no checklist guarantees immunity from compromise.
CISA recommends MFA, with phishing-resistant methods preferred where available. A second factor helps only when recovery and approval practices also remain secure.

web-design.note: MDN core modules cover semantic HTML, CSS, layout, accessible interfaces, and related tools. Use these technical references alongside actual device, keyboard, and accessibility testing; documentation alone does not determine legal compliance.

WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 generally specifies at least 4.5:1 contrast for ordinary text and 3:1 for qualifying large text, with defined exceptions. Measure actual colors and consult the full criterion; WCAG is a standard, not a universal statement of law.

javascript-foundations.note: MDN documents JavaScript language and browser behavior. Test sample code in a safe environment and validate assumptions; a working tutorial does not establish production security.

data-spreadsheets.note: Check formulas, references, source ranges, and expected results. Spreadsheet features differ by application and version; numeric scenarios in this lesson are illustrative rather than research or market data.
Protect access and use the minimum necessary data. Applicable privacy, contractual, and retention duties depend on the data and organization; this lesson does not claim one law covers every dataset.

responsible-ai.note: NIST AI RMF is voluntary risk-management guidance addressing AI trustworthiness and risk. It does not certify a tool or replace applicable privacy, employment, consumer-protection, intellectual-property, or other law.

personal-finance.note: Use CFPB's official credit-report guidance and dispute resources to understand the process. Check the actual record and relevant provider instructions rather than relying on promises of guaranteed credit repair.
